passages.title: Solomon’s Building of the Temple.
passages.text: The temple is to be a fit place for God to dwell among his people.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 3:1–17
passages.text: The Chronicler’s actual account of the construction of the temple is much briefer than the account in 1 Kings 6 . The temple did not function as a place of congregational worship. Only priests would have been admitted to the temple itself. Only on the Day of Atonement could the high priest enter the Most Holy Place.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 3:8–13
passages.text: The **Most Holy Place** was the secret, cube-shaped room in which the ark of the covenant would be finally deposited ( 5:7 ). The **cherubim** were angelic beings that combined human and animal features (see Ezek. 10:14 ; 41:18–19 ). On the temple construction, see note on 1 Kings 6:14–35 .

passages.title: 2 Chron. 3:15–17
passages.text: **thirty-five cubits high**. Probably the combined heights of the pillars (see note on 1 Kings 7:15–21 ; see 1 Kings 7:15 ; 2 Kings 25:17 ). **Jachin** (“he establishes”); **Boaz** (“in him is strength”).

notes.text: Mount Zion is identified here with **Mount Moriah**, where Abraham was commanded to offer Isaac ( Gen. 22:2 ).
Compare 1 Kings 6:1 . Depending on which chronology is followed, this may have been in either 966 or 959 b.c.

**120 cubits**. The Septuagint and other ancient versions of the OT suggest that the **vestibule** was actually 20 cubits (30 feet/9.1 m) high. The Hebrew text lacks the word “cubits,” so the precise height is uncertain.
**Parvaim**. Possibly a place in northeastern Arabia.
The inclusion of the **veil** connected the temple with the Mosaic tabernacle ( Ex. 26:31–35 ).
